problem: Given the hyperboloid of two sheets $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}=-1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$

feedback.problem: Given the hyperboloid of one sheet  $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{5}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{5} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-1 & =\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{5} \\ (z-1)^{2} & =5(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-1) \\ (z-1) & =\pm \sqrt{5(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

  

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-1 & \ge 0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8} & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}=1$, including its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}\ge 1}.
$$
